findings.source_quote: οἱ δὲ τὸν Θεὸν ἐγνωκότες καὶ τὰ μεγαλεῖα αὐτοῦ ἑωρακότες καὶ πονηρευόμενοι δισσῶς κολασθήσονται καὶ ἀποθανοῦνται εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα.
findings.english_quote: Retain each group’s stated responsibility, possibility or exclusion of repentance, and the life/death consequences.
findings.issue: The theological metadata attributes statements about the possibility or exclusion of repentance to this section, although the selected source contains no such statements. It distinguishes responsibility and punishment, not opportunities for repentance. The accompanying rationale about difficult entry likewise describes material absent from this unit.
findings.suggested_revision: Revise the metadata to describe this section’s actual distinctions: knowledge of God, evil conduct, differentiated punishment, death, and the church’s purification. Remove claims about repentance opportunities and difficult entry unless explicitly identified as material from another section. Review the replacement metadata afresh.

findings.source_quote: ἐὰν οὖν ὁ ἀγαπῶν ἀγαθοποιεῖν πονηρεύηται, οὐ δοκεῖ πλείονα πονηρίαν ποιεῖν παρὰ τὸν μὴ γινώσκοντα τὸν Θεόν;
findings.english_quote: If someone who loves to do good[b] does evil, is that not greater evil than what someone who does not know God does?
findings.issue: The simplified question omits δοκεῖ, changing an appeal to how the person’s conduct appears or is judged into an unqualified question about its being greater evil. The standard edition preserves this component with “seem.”
findings.suggested_revision: Proposed wording for fresh review: “So if someone who loves to do good does evil, does that person not seem to do greater evil than someone who does not know God?” Retain the footnote marker.

findings.source_quote: διὰ τοῦτο οἱ μὴ ἐγνωκ⸢ό⸣τες Θεὸν καὶ πονηρευόμενοι κεκριμένοι εἰσὶν εἰς θάνατον
findings.english_quote: People who do evil without knowing God have been condemned to death.
findings.issue: The explicit causal connection διὰ τοῦτο, “for this reason,” is omitted. This leaves the condemnation statement disconnected from the preceding comparison of responsibility.
findings.suggested_revision: Proposed wording for fresh review: “That is why people who do evil without knowing God have been condemned to death.”

findings.source_quote: ἵνα πᾶσα ψυχὴ πεποιθυῖα ἐπὶ τὸν Κύριον ἀκούσασα δοξάσῃ τὸ μέγα καὶ θαυμαστὸν καὶ ἔνδοξον ὄνομα αὐτοῦ.
findings.english_quote: Then every person who trusts in the Lord can hear and glorify his great, wonderful and glorious name.
findings.issue: “Then ... can” replaces the stated purpose of the requested explanation with temporal sequence and ability. The source says the explanation is requested so that every trusting person, upon hearing, may glorify the Lord’s name.
findings.suggested_revision: Proposed wording for fresh review: “Explain what each mountain means and what its actions are, so that every person who trusts in the Lord may hear and glorify his great, wonderful and glorious name.”

findings.source_quote: οἱ δὲ τὸν Θεὸν ἐγνωκότες καὶ τὰ μεγαλεῖα αὐτοῦ ἑωρακότες καὶ πονηρευόμενοι δισσῶς κολασθήσονται καὶ ἀποθανοῦνται εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα.
findings.english_quote: Retain comparative responsibility, distinct repentance claims, difficult entry, allegiance and life/death imagery; preserve all substantive alternative notes.
findings.issue: The simplification metadata claims to preserve distinct repentance claims and difficult entry, neither of which occurs in this selected section. The theological metadata independently makes the same unsupported attribution concerning repentance possibilities or exclusions.
findings.suggested_revision: Revise both metadata blocks to describe only the distinctions present here: comparative responsibility, punishment and death, exclusion of evil people, purification, unity, and the concluding request. Remove the claims about repentance and difficult entry. Review replacement metadata afresh.

summary: Both editions require revision. The standard reader text covers the selected source faithfully, but its theological metadata describes claims absent from this section. Independent review of the simplified text also finds losses of the judgment wording, causal connection, and purpose construction. The disclosed God and “loves to do good” selections are consistent with the supplied bounded project reports; the restoration and bracketed dialogue attribution are identified as editorial. This review does not authenticate unseen manuscripts or certify exhaustive collation. All proposed replacements require fresh review.
